abstract: In Landau's local method for Beurling zeta functions in the extended sense, $F(s)=\exp(\int_{1-}^\infty x^{-s}\,dm(x))$ with $dm\ge 0$, Broucke and Révész derive local disk bounds down to the triple-logarithmic radius $\delta_0(\tau)$ and, under polynomial growth $\psi\equiv 1$ and $\varphi(t)=C\log(t+e)+C_0$, bound the multiplicity of a zero on a fixed line $\sigma=b\in(1/2,1)$ by $O_b(\log\gamma)$. Using rescaled Diamond–Montgomery–Vorhauer factors at heights $\gamma_k=\exp(4^k)$, we construct extended Beurling models satisfying all hypotheses of their Theorems 3.1 and 5.4 that carry either a companion zero of multiplicity $N_k\asymp\log\gamma_k/\log\log\gamma_k$ next to a simple zero on $\sigma=b\in(4/5,1)$ (within $\log\log\gamma_k$ of their upper bound, with $|F'(\rho_k)|^{-2}=\gamma_k^{2\kappa-o(1)}$), or a cluster of $N_k+1$ simple zeros on $\sigma=b\in(1/2,1)$ obeying a $T^{o(1)}$ zero-density bound on every fixed abscissa and a Littlewood-order local strip bound while forcing the sub-$\delta_0$ logarithmic potential to satisfy $I(\rho_{k,0};\gamma_k)/\log\gamma_k\to 1$. Conversely, positivity of the distributional prime density forces the kernel dilation scale to satisfy $(1-b)a_k\ge\log(N_k+1)-\log(4M_0 e^{1-b})-O((\log q_k)^2/q_k)$ across narrow clusters, and for super-exponential scales $a_\ell=e^{2q_\ell}$ yields a sharp distributional-positivity threshold $\Lambda_c$ enclosed within $\log(2n)-9q^3 e^{-2q}\le\Lambda_c\le\log(2n)-\log(1-e^{-a})$ (without analytic product continuation past $\operatorname{Re}s=b$). We also show that the secondary zero towers of these specific DMV cluster models violate the Riemann–von Mangoldt strip-count asymptotic, give counterexamples separating positivity from structural bounds, and establish sufficient summability conditions and contrasting convergence examples on a safe half-strip. RH is treated here as open; nothing is claimed about the zeros of $\zeta(s)$, and discretization to generalized primes is not addressed.
author: lihongmin
change_summary:
- Appendix A, Proposition A.1(ii) and equation (A.3): replaced the unshifted condition $\gamma_\ell>2|t|+2$ (which fails for large negative $\sigma$, e.g. at $b=3/4,\ell=5,s=-3\gamma_5$) with the point-dependent threshold $\gamma_\ell>2(|t|+|b-\sigma|)+2$, wrote out the bound $|a_\ell(s-\rho_{\ell,j})|\le 2\gamma_\ell^3$ explicitly, and distinguished the base-free partial products $\prod_{\ell=k_0(b)}^M P_\ell(s)$ (exceptional zero set $Z_{\mathrm{fin}}$) from the full partial products $F_0(s)\prod_{\ell=k_0(b)}^M P_\ell(s)$ including $F_0(s)=s/(s-1)$ (exceptional zero set $Z_{\mathrm{fin}}\cup\{0\}$ since $F_0(0)=0$ and $0\notin Z_{\mathrm{fin}}$).
- Abstract and Section 1: replaced 'characterize product convergence' with wording describing sufficient summability conditions and contrasting examples; highlighted in the abstract, Theorem 1.3, Proposition 1.4, and the Relation to RH paragraph that Theorem 1.3 concerns distributional positivity on $(0,\infty)$ without the analytic continuation of Theorem 1.1 (by Proposition A.1) and that Proposition 1.4 excludes the particular DMV secondary-zero towers from the classical strip-count asymptotic rather than excluding every conceivable positive-measure cluster construction.
- Section 2 and References: explicitly distinguished Broucke, Debruyne, and Révész [15, Theorem 3.2] (prescribing only finite zero multisets while introducing an auxiliary pole $(s/(s-\delta))^M$ in $\operatorname{Re}s>0$), and corrected the published title and issue number of Révész [9] (Mathematika 68 (2022), no. 4, 1045–1072, doi:10.1112/mtk.12156) to 'Density estimates for the zeros of the Beurling $\zeta$ function in the critical strip'.
- Theorem 1.1(a), Section 4.2 Step 4, and Section 5 proofs: specified 'for sufficiently large $k$' in the isolation clause of Theorem 1.1(a) and Section 4.2 Step 4; replaced '$|W_{k,\alpha}|\le 4$' with the integral bound $\int_I W_{k,\alpha}(t)\,dt\le 2$ at the end of the proof of Lemma 5.2; and corrected the inline evaluation of $(8/3)\log(a^4)$ at $v=a^4$ in the proof of Theorem 1.3 from $32q/3$ to $64q/3$.
- Section 7 and Supplement (verify_envelope_and_thresholds.py, supplement README, recorded outputs, and CONTENTS.sha256): added an outward interval verification of the corrected threshold and equation (A.3) together with a sixth fault-injection negative control rejecting the unshifted condition at $b=3/4,\ell=5,s=-3\gamma_5$, clarified that the Lemma 3.3 interval enclosures bound the series-truncation upper-bound proxies rather than the smaller true variations, regenerated outputs, and refreshed CONTENTS.sha256.
title: Littlewood-size zero clusters in Landau's local method: a Diamond–Montgomery–Vorhauer construction and the scale it costs
